history.summary: A 700 sqft 1BR near Aljunied MRT (360m) at a low $999 psf and $699k quantum — the cheapest entry in the batch and well below the $1,572 median. But the headline 9.78% appreciation rests on just 7 transactions, far below any reliability threshold, so the value signal is unverified.
history.rating_rationale: The attractive surface — $999 psf vs $1,572 median, $699k entry (low quantum = broad buyer pool), Aljunied EW9 360m — is undercut by the data quality: only 7 URA transactions underpin both the 9.78% CAGR and the $1,572 median, so neither figure is dependable (the rubric flags <10 txns as concerning and reliability needs 50+). The roomy 700 sqft for a '1BR' and very low PSF suggest a non-standard/older-stock layout that explains part of the discount. Low quantum and good transit keep it off Avoid, but a 7-txn series means I cannot confirm this is genuine value rather than a thinly-traded outlier — Neutral pending real transaction depth.

history.summary: Algo's #1 (979/1000) on a -46% age-adjusted discount, but the cheapness is a data artifact: the listing's 700sqft/$998psf does not fit a 50-unit project where 1-beds are 377-484sqft and recent resales average ~$1,507psf ($999-$1,814 range). psf_cohort_txns=1 = no real comparable.
history.rating_rationale: Recent Avant Residences resales average ~$1,507 psf (range $999-$1,814 over the last 12 months); this listing's $998.57 psf sits at the absolute floor of that range. A 700 sqft '1-bed' is inconsistent with the project's actual 1-bed sizes (377-484 sqft) - 700sqft is a 2-bed/2+1 format here, so the unit is being scored against the wrong (1-bed) cohort, producing the -34.4% psf_premium_vs_cohort on just 1 comparable txn. The -46.1% age-adjusted discount and 9.78% CAGR ride on only 7 txns. It is 99LH from 2012 (~85yrs left). D14 is OCR-adjacent (favorable forward region prior ~+4%), and if the $998psf and 700sqft are both real this is a genuinely cheap 2-bed-sized unit near Aljunied/Mountbatten MRT - but the sqft/bed mismatch and thin cohort mean I cannot confirm the bargain. Neutral, low confidence pending verification of actual unit size on the listing.

history.summary: The volume product of this 50-unit block: studios/1BR+S from 377-700sqft, ~$690-790k quantum, 320m to Aljunied MRT. Real URA rents give ~4.6% gross yield and the asking psf sits ~10% under the age-adjusted district median — but the project has 7 resales in 5 years and small-unit psf is still below its 2018 peak, so this is a yield hold with no demonstrated capital growth.
history.rating_rationale: Honest yield play, not a growth asset. The MMR 768 leans on a 9.78% CAGR that is a mix artifact (ground-floor $986psf 2021 base); the verifiable small-unit trend is ~3%/yr off a 2024 base and $1,572 Apr-2026 < $1,826 Jun-2018 peak. ~4.6% yield near MRT is solid for D14, but exit liquidity (~2.8%/yr turnover) and Geylang-fringe stigma mean you may give back the discount on exit. The -9.6% relative-value cushion is fair compensation, not an edge.

Among 1BR types the 484sqft 1BR+S (18 units, biggest cohort) is the most defensible buy/exit; avoid paying full psf for 700sqft 1BR+S ground-floor/PES variants (outdoor space in the sqft). Stack-facing map unverified — check unit orientation vs Aljunied Rd on viewing.

history.summary: Portal-labelled 3BR is actually the 936sqft 2BR+Study DUAL-KEY (two self-contained sub-units), of which only 4 exist (#02-02 to #05-02, stack 02 floors 2-5). The $1.29M listing at $1,378psf is the cheapest psf in the project and -17.9% vs age-adjusted median; the dual-key format can out-earn the single-tenancy rent estimate, but a 4-unit cohort means there is essentially no resale market to price against.
history.rating_rationale: Cheapest psf entry with a real dual-key income angle (two tenancies near MRT could beat the $5,784 single-let estimate, which itself looks optimistic vs SRX large-unit psf rents). But the entire thesis rests on 4 units with zero recent transactions — psf_cohort_txns=0 — so both the 'discount' and the exit price are unpriceable. A $1.3-1.4M quantum locked into a no-facility Geylang-fringe boutique with ~no comparables is a liquidity trap even if the carry is good. Only worth pursuing at a clear discount ($1,378psf end, not $1,496) and with dual-key rent evidence in hand.
